tools.description:
Execute a `bash` command. Use this for shell semantics — pipes, env, processes, git, package managers, build/test runners, anything genuinely interactive or multi-step.

**Translate these to a dedicated tool instead:**
- `cat` / `head` / `tail` (known path) → `Read`
- `sed` / `awk` (in-place edit) → `Edit`
- `echo > file` / `cat <<EOF` → `Write`
- `find` / recursive `ls` to locate files by name pattern → `Glob` (plain `ls <known-directory>` is fine for listing a directory)
- `grep` / `rg` (search file contents) → `Grep`
- `echo` / `printf` (talk to the user) → just output text directly

The dedicated tools render in the per-tool permission UI and keep raw stdout out of the conversation; that is why they are worth reaching for whenever one fits.

**Output:**
The stdout and stderr will be combined and returned as a string. The output may be truncated if it is too long. If the command exits non-zero, the output ends with a `Command failed with exit code: N` line; a command killed by its timeout or interrupted by the user ends with its own message instead.

Background execution is disabled for this agent. Do not set `run_in_background=true`.

**Guidelines for safety and security:**
- Each shell tool call will be executed in a fresh shell environment. The shell variables, current working directory changes, and the shell history is not preserved between calls. To run a command in a particular directory, pass the `cwd` argument (or use absolute paths) rather than relying on a `cd` from an earlier call.
- The tool call will return after the command is finished. You shall not use this tool to execute an interactive command or a command that may run forever. For possibly long-running commands, set the `timeout` argument in seconds. The default is 60s; foreground commands allow up to 300s; a foreground command that hits its timeout is killed.
- Avoid using `..` to access files or directories outside of the working directory.
- Avoid modifying files outside of the working directory unless explicitly instructed to do so.
- Never run commands that require superuser privileges unless explicitly instructed to do so.

**Guidelines for efficiency:**
- Use `&&` to chain commands that genuinely depend on each other, e.g. `npm install && npm test`. Independent read-only commands (separate `git show`, `ls`, or status checks) should be issued as separate parallel Bash calls in one response, not chained into a single call — chaining serializes their execution and mixes their output. Do not stitch outputs together with `echo` separators.
- Use `;` to run commands sequentially regardless of success/failure
- Use `||` for conditional execution (run second command only if first fails)
- Use pipe operations (`|`) and redirections (`>`, `>>`) to chain input and output between commands
- Always quote file paths containing spaces with double quotes (e.g., cd "/path with spaces/")
- Compose multi-step logic in a single call with `if` / `case` / `for` / `while` control flows.
- Do not set `run_in_background=true`; background task management tools are not available.

**Commands available:**
The following common command categories are usually available. Availability still depends on the host, so when in doubt run `which <command>` first to confirm a command exists before relying on it.
- Navigation and inspection: `ls`, `pwd`, `cd`, `stat`, `file`, `du`, `df`, `tree`
- File and directory management: `cp`, `mv`, `rm`, `mkdir`, `touch`, `ln`, `chmod`, `chown`
- Text and data processing: `wc`, `sort`, `uniq`, `cut`, `tr`, `diff`, `xargs`
- Archives and compression: `tar`, `gzip`, `gunzip`, `zip`, `unzip`
- Networking and transfer: `curl`, `wget`, `ping`, `ssh`, `scp`
- Version control: `git`; for GitHub-hosted work (PRs, issues, CI runs, API queries) prefer the `gh` CLI when installed — it carries the user's GitHub auth and can return structured JSON
- Process and system: `ps`, `kill`, `top`, `env`, `date`, `uname`, `whoami`
- Language and package toolchains: `node`, `npm`, `pnpm`, `yarn`, `python`, `pip` (use whichever the project actually relies on)

tools.description:
Find files by glob pattern, sorted by modification time (most recent first).

Powered by ripgrep. Respects `.gitignore`, `.ignore`, and `.rgignore` by default — set `include_ignored` to also match ignored files (e.g. build outputs, `node_modules`). Sensitive files (such as `.env`) are always filtered out. Matches are files only — directories themselves are never listed; to find a directory, glob for a file inside it (e.g. `**/fixtures/**`).

Good patterns:
- `*.ts` — all files matching an extension, at any depth below the search root (a bare pattern without `/` matches recursively)
- `src/*.ts` — files directly inside `src/` (one level, not recursive)
- `src/**/*.ts` — recursive walk with a subdirectory anchor and extension
- `**/*.py` — recursive walk from the search root for an extension
- `*.{ts,tsx}` — brace expansion is supported
- `{src,test}/**/*.ts` — cartesian brace expansion is supported too

# richgo

Rich-Go will enrich `go test` outputs with text decorations.

[![asciicast](https://asciinema.org/a/99810.png)](https://asciinema.org/a/99810)

## Description

richgo is a command-line tool that adds color and formatting to the output of Go's `go test` command, making test results easier to read and understand.

## Installation

### Using go get

```
go get -u github.com/kyoh86/richgo
```

### Using homebrew

```
brew install kyoh86/tap/richgo
```

### Using asdf

```
asdf plugin add richgo
asdf install richgo 0.3.6
```

## Usage

### Basic Usage

```sh
richgo test ./...
```

### In an existing pipeline

If your build scripts expect to interact with the standard output format of `go test` (for instance, if you're using [go-junit-report](https://github.com/jstemmer/go-junit-report)), you'll need to use the `testfilter` subcommand of `richgo`.

For example:

```sh
go test ./... | tee >(richgo testfilter) | go-junit-report
```

This will "tee" the output of the standard `go test` run into a `richgo testfilter` process as well as passing the original output to `go-junit-report`.

All probes complete and temp dirs cleaned up. Here is the full behavioral spec for Domain 1.

# DOMAIN 1 REPORT — default-config `testfilter` line classification & rendering

Setup: empty CWD (no `.richstyle*`), `RICHGO_FORCE_COLOR=1`, input piped to `/workspace/executable testfilter`. Escapes written as `ESC[..m`. Reset is always `ESC[0m`.

## Global structure

- Output line skeleton: `STYLE? LABEL| indent CONTENT ESC[0m? \n`, where `LABEL` is padded to **5 chars**, immediately followed by `|` (no space): `PASS |`, `FAIL |`, `SKIP |`, `START|`, `BUILD|`.
- Unrecognized ("plain") lines get prefix `     | ` — exactly **5 spaces + `| `** — i.e. the `|` sits in the same column as for labels.
- Input is processed line-by-line; `\n` and a trailing `\r` are stripped (CRLF input renders as plain LF output). An unterminated final line still gets a `\n` appended.
- Completely empty input lines (`\n` only) produce **zero output bytes** (dropped). Whitespace-only lines are plain lines (`   \n` → `     |    \n`).
- Exit code is **0 in all cases** (FAIL content, empty input, etc.).

## Context-color state machine (important!)

Every styled status line sets a persistent "current style". All subsequent **plain** lines are wrapped in that style (including their `     | ` prefix) until the next status line changes it:

- `=== RUN`/`--- SKIP`/`? [no test files]` → `ESC[90m`
- `--- PASS`/`ok` → `ESC[32m`
- `--- FAIL`/`FAIL<pkg>` → `ESC[31mESC[1m`
- `# <pkg>` → `ESC[33mESC[1m`
- Hidden lines (bare `PASS`/`FAIL`) and blank lines do **not** change it. Initial state = no style.

Example: `--- FAIL: TestX (0.00s)\nlog line\n` →
`ESC[31mESC[1mFAIL | X (0.00s)ESC[0m\n` then `ESC[31mESC[1m     | log lineESC[0m\n`.
Context persists across blank lines; `ok ...` after FAIL switches context to green, etc.

## Category 1 — `=== RUN` → START

- Regex ≈ `^=== RUN   (Test.*)$` — **exactly 3 spaces**, column 0, name must start with `Test`.
- Output: `ESC[90mSTART|` + N spaces + `<name minus leading "Test">` + `ESC[0m\n`, where **N = 1 + 2×(number of `/` in the name)**.
  - `=== RUN   TestX` → `ESC[90mSTART| XESC[0m\n`
  - `=== RUN   TestX/A/B` → `START|     X/A/B` (5 spaces)
  - `=== RUN   Test` → `ESC[90mSTART| ESC[0m\n` (name strips to empty; the 1 space remains)
  - `=== RUN   Test X` → `START|  X` (remainder ` X` kept verbatim)
- NOT matched (→ plain): 1/2/4 spaces or tab after `RUN`; any leading indentation; names starting `Example`/`Benchmark`/`Fuzz`/`Foo`.
- `=== PAUSE   TestX`, `=== CONT   TestX`, `=== NAME   TestX` are **not** recognized → plain lines.

## Category 2 — test result lines `--- PASS/FAIL/SKIP`

- Regex ≈ `^( *)--- (PASS|FAIL|SKIP): (Test.*)$` (space after colon required; name must start `Test`; time NOT required — `--- PASS: TestX` matches and `--- PASS: TestX (0.00s) trailing` keeps everything after the name verbatim).
- **Input indentation (spaces) is discarded**; output indent is recomputed from slashes exactly like RUN: N = 1 + 2×depth spaces after `|`.
  - `--- PASS: TestX (0.00s)` → `ESC[32mPASS | X (0.00s)ESC[0m\n`
  - `    --- PASS: TestX/Sub (0.00s)` → `ESC[32mPASS |   X/Sub (0.00s)ESC[0m\n` (3 spaces)
  - `--- FAIL: TestX (0.01s)` → `ESC[31mESC[1mFAIL | X (0.01s)ESC[0m\n`
  - `--- SKIP: TestX (0.00s)` → `ESC[90mSKIP | X (0.00s)ESC[0m\n`
- **Tab-indented fallback**: if the leading whitespace contains a tab (`\t--- FAIL: TestX (0.00s)`, ` \t--- PASS: TestX ...`), the label/style is applied but the **entire original line is kept as content** (no Test-strip, no reindent): `ESC[31mESC[1mFAIL | \t--- FAIL: TestX (0.00s)ESC[0m\n`. Still requires `: ` + `Test` (`\t--- PASS: Foo` and `\t--- PASS:TestX` → plain). Sets context normally.
- NOT matched (→ plain): `--- BENCH:`, `--- PASS: Foo`, `--- PASS:TestX`, `foo --- FAIL: bar`.

## Category 3 — package `ok` / `FAIL` lines

- `ok` recognized forms (separator after `ok` = spaces and/or tabs): `ok  pkg 0.002s`, `ok  pkg (cached)`, `ok  pkg 0.002s [no tests to run]`, `ok  pkg [no tests to run]`, trailing whitespace tolerated. Time must be `[\d.]+s` — `1m0.5s` is NOT matched (→ plain); `0.002s (cached)` (time + cached) NOT matched.
- Normal rendering: `ESC[32mPASS | <pkg> ESC[0m\n` — note the **single trailing space before the reset**; time, `(cached)`, `[no tests to run]` are dropped. E.g. `ok  \texample.com/p\t0.002s` → `ESC[32mPASS | example.com/p ESC[0m\n`.
- **ANOMALY (exact bytes)**: bare `ok  pkg` with no time/bracket/trailing-ws → `ESC[32mPASS | example.com/p\n ESC[0m` — i.e. newline *inside* the style, then a space, then reset, and **no trailing newline**. Same with unterminated input. Context is still set to green. This is reproducible mid-stream (next line's bytes follow immediately after `ESC[0m`).
- `FAIL` package lines: matched when the line ends with time or `[build failed]`: `FAIL\tpkg\t0.002s` → `ESC[31mESC[1mFAIL | \texample.com/p\t0.002sESC[0m\n`; `FAIL\tpkg [build failed]` → same pattern — **everything after `FAIL` is kept verbatim** (separator tab/space, time, bracket). `FAIL pkg` / `FAIL\tpkg` without time, and `FAIL\tpkg\t[setup failed]` → plain.

## Category 4 — `? pkg [no test files]` → SKIP

- Requires the line to **end exactly** at `]` (trailing space → plain). Other brackets (`[setup failed]`) → plain.
- `?   \texample.com/p\t[no test files]` → `ESC[90mSKIP | example.com/p\t[no test files]ESC[0m\n` (leading ws after `?` consumed; pkg and tab kept). Sets context 90.

## Category 5 — build errors `# pkg` → BUILD

- Matched: `^# <pkg>$` and `^# <pkg> [<anything>]$`. NOT matched: `#pkg`, `# pkg ` (trailing space), `# pkg extra`.
- With bracket: `ESC[33mESC[1mBUILD| example.com/p [example.com/p.test]ESC[0m\n` (normal).
- **ANOMALY**: bare `# pkg` → `ESC[33mESC[1mBUILD| example.com/p\nESC[0m` (newline inside style, reset after, **no trailing newline**, no space). Sets context 33+1.

## Hidden lines

- Bare `PASS`, `FAIL`, `PASS `, `FAIL ` (with trailing space, with or without trailing newline) → **zero output bytes**, no context change.
- Bare `SKIP` is NOT hidden → plain line `     | SKIP`.

## Plain lines & file:line highlighting

- Anything else → `     | <original line>\n`, wrapped in context style if one is active.
- Inside plain lines, a global highlight is applied to `file.go:NN[:MM]` references: path ending in `.go` (any non-space prefix incl `./`, `/abs/`) → `ESC[36m`, the `:N` or `:N:M` part → `ESC[35m`, each followed by `ESC[0m`. Multiple matches per line all highlighted; `foo.txt:12:` and `a.go:abc:` not highlighted; `a.go:1:2:3: x` highlights only `:1:2`.
  - No context: `./main.go:3:2: undefined: x` → `     | ESC[36m./main.goESC[0mESC[35m:3:2ESC[0m: undefined: x\n`
  - With context, the context style is **re-emitted** after each nested reset: `ESC[31mESC[1m     |     ESC[36mfoo_test.goESC[0mESC[35m:12ESC[0mESC[31mESC[1m: msgESC[0m\n`
- Benchmark result lines (`BenchmarkX-8\t100\t1234 ns/op`), `panic: ...`, `testing: warning: no tests to run`, compiler lines, test log lines — all plain (with the highlight rule above where applicable).

## No-color mode (no TTY, `RICHGO_FORCE_COLOR` unset)

Pure pass-through: input copied **verbatim** (no Test-strip, no hiding, no prefixes), then **exactly one extra `\n` is appended at EOF**. Observed: `line one\nline two\n` → `line one\nline two\n\n`; empty input → `\n`; `abc` → `abc\n`; `PASS\n` → `PASS\n\n`.

## Style codes summary (default config)

- START: `ESC[90m`; PASS: `ESC[32m`; FAIL: `ESC[31mESC[1m`; SKIP: `ESC[90m`; BUILD: `ESC[33mESC[1m`; file: `ESC[36m`; line numbers: `ESC[35m`; reset: `ESC[0m`.
- Labels (5-wide, `|` immediately after): `START`, `PASS `, `FAIL `, `SKIP `, `BUILD`.
- Test prefix stripping: literal leading `Test` removed from the captured name only (first component; `/Sub` parts untouched); consistent with `leaveTestPrefix=false`.

Not covered (left to other domains): `labelType` variants, config-file overrides, the underlying cause of the two `\n`-inside-style anomalies (`ok pkg` bare, `# pkg` bare) — exact bytes documented above are authoritative.
